subject: ventures/ghostwriter-book-quote-calculator
professional: a working book ghostwriter (or collaborative-author agent) who quotes five-figure nonfiction and memoir projects and has been burned by revision creep

evidence.correctness: Ran `node -e` against calc.mjs with DEFAULTS and recomputed by hand: drafting 60000/350 = 171.43 h, interviews 20 x 2 = 40, research 15, revisions 2 x 0.1 x 171.43 = 34.29, management 12, total 272.71 h; x $75 x 1.25 = $25,566.96; + $600 expenses = $26,166.96, which matches analyze().invoice (26166.964). A second hand case (platformFee 0.2, rushPremium 0.5, no confidentiality, no expenses) gives 272.714 x 75 x 1.5 / 0.8 = $38,350.45, matching. Budget words at a $20,000 budget: (20000 - 600)/93.75 = 206.93 h, minus 67 fixed h, divided by 1.2/350 h per word = 40,813 words, matching budgetWords. The market cross-check is weak: primary EFA and Reedsy rate pages gave no numbers (EFA page is a survey form), so only secondary summaries were available (WebSearch, 2026-11-10: EFA nonfiction about $0.33 to $0.50 per word, $125 per 250-word page for memoir); the default $0.436 per word and $109 per page sit inside that, a partial confirmation. Two outputs a user would act on are wrong or inconsistent. (1) extraRound = 0.1 x 171.43 x $75 = $1,285.71 omits the confidentiality premium that the quoted fee charges on every hour, so the number the page tells the writer to 'put in the agreement' prices a round at $75 an hour while the main quote prices hours at $93.75; with the default 25% premium it is $321 (20%) short. (2) atBudget = $71.14 is shown against the $75 target, but the same formula at the full quote returns $93.75, so the budget hourly is not on the same basis as the target and understates how much the discount costs. Also verified rejected input: wordCount 'string' and negative overrun return warnings and a null result.
evidence.completeness: README and page claims checked by running calc.mjs: hours breakdown (works), flat fee (works), per-word and per-250-word-page rate (works), deposit and milestone schedule (works, sums to invoice), extra revision round price (works but see correctness), real hourly under overrun (works: 75.00 at 25% overrun, premium cancels), client-budget hourly and words bought (works), size grid (5 rows, middle equals invoice), CSV export (11 rows), example loader, usage counters switchable off (usage.mjs tests pass). No stub or TODO found in calc.mjs, index.html, usage.mjs. The FAQ on the page, schema.org JSON-LD, robots.txt and sitemap.xml exist. The served page https://marisstella.app/ghostwriter-book-quote-calculator/ returned HTTP 200. Not checked: pixel rendering in a browser; no headless browser was run.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture directory: 28 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail (calc 15, page 7, usage 6). Six hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with `git checkout -- calc.mjs` and the tree confirmed clean with `git status`: platform fee gross-up `/` to `*` at line 52 (caught, 2 failures); dropping revisionRounds from revisions at line 42 (caught, 2 failures); dropping interview overhead at line 39 (caught, 1 failure); removing the platform fee from the budget-words calculation at line 104 (SURVIVED, 28 pass); doubling the extra-revision-round price at line 108 (SURVIVED, no test reads extraRound); Math.round to Math.floor on the milestone count at line 64 (SURVIVED). Half the mutations survived, including the whole extra-revision-round output the page tells users to write into a contract. The budget-words test uses the default platformFee of 0, so a fee error there cannot show.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (129 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, the module script in index.html. Pure functions, a single DEFAULTS table drives both inputs and tests, input is validated before computing (non-finite, negative, platformFee >= 1, deposit > 1), explicit warnings rather than silent fallbacks, milestone count capped at 60, no network calls (a test greps for fetch and beacons). Defects: platformFee is accepted at 0.9999 and returns a $261 million invoice with no warning (line 82 only blocks >= 1); `milestones` of 0 or 0.4 silently becomes 1 and 0; deposit of exactly 1 yields zero-dollar milestones without a note; extraRound ignores the confidentiality premium (line 108). The grid recomputes hours per word count but keeps management and research fixed, which is sensible.
evidence.claims: README Model section matches the code (checked each of three formulas against calc.mjs lines 41 to 59). Page and README say the defaults are placeholders, not market rates, and a test (page.test.mjs) asserts the phrase. The FAQ states quotes 'commonly run from low five figures to well over $100,000'; that is consistent with the secondary sources found but is unsourced on the page, and the page does flag the figures as not market data. Disclaimer, privacy and best-effort text present and tested. llms.txt points to the duncan-haywood.github.io address; the build rewrites hosts at deploy, so this was not filed as a defect (source-only). README says 'Effective hourly = (invoice x (1 - commission) - expenses) / hours actually worked', which matches the code, but the page's 'what you would earn at their budget' reading is on a different basis from the target hourly (see correctness). VENTURE.yaml stage is honestly 'prototype' with an untested hypothesis.
evidence.fitness: Walked a ghostwriter's job: enter a 60,000-word memoir, 20 interview hours, 25% confidentiality premium, a client budget of $20,000. The tool returns a $26,167 flat fee, $0.44 per word, a three-milestone schedule, 40,813 words that the budget buys and a real hourly of $75 if the job overruns by 25%. That answers 'can you do it for less' with a shorter scope, which is the stated job. The writer can finish the quote, but two numbers (extra round, hourly at budget) would be copied into a negotiation and are off by the premium. There is no way to enter more than one rate by phase (research and interviews at a lower rate) and no kill fee or royalty line, which the page lists as not modelled.
evidence.domain: Compared against how working ghostwriters quote (EFA convention of a 250-word page, hours-first pricing with flat-fee presentation, a deposit of 25 to 50 percent, milestone payments, and a priced revision limit). The structure is what a practitioner would build: interview time and revision rounds are the costs that sink flat fees and both are explicit. Departures: drafting rate of 350 finished words per hour is a placeholder (the page says so), the confidentiality premium is taken as a flat 25 percent with no source, and the extra-round price drops the premium. No treatment of an expansion or reduction of the word count after contract, which is the usual real overrun.

defects.what: The extra-revision-round price omits the confidentiality premium that every hour of the quoted fee carries, so the figure the page says to put in the agreement is 20% below the quote's own rate at the default premium ($1,286 vs $1,607).
No test reads extraRound at all, so doubling or deleting the number passes 28 tests.

Hourly at the client's budget ($71.14) is compared to the base target ($75) though the quote's own at-plan hourly is $93.75 with the premium, so the discount's cost is understated; the budget-words calculation is also untested with a platform fee (mutation survived).
Platform fee 0.9999 is accepted and yields a $261 million quote with no warning; only >= 1 is blocked.
Milestone count is rounded silently (0 or 0.4 becomes 1) and the rounding direction is untested (mutation survived).
Drafting speed, confidentiality premium and the 'low five figures to well over $100,000' FAQ range have no cited rate source; primary EFA and Reedsy pages were not usable as a check.

verdict: A small, honest, well-structured hours-first quote tool whose main arithmetic (hours, fee, gross-up, schedule, words a budget buys) recomputes exactly by hand and whose page, disclaimer and placeholders are truthful. It does not meet the bar: correctness is 2 because the extra-revision-round price, which the page tells the writer to put into a contract, leaves out the confidentiality premium and is 20% low at defaults, and the hourly-at-budget is on a different basis from the target; verification is 2 because three of six seeded bugs survived 28 green tests, including the extra-round output and platform-fee handling in the budget calculation. External validation was limited to secondary summaries of EFA rates because the primary pages were not readable. Scores are the state before any fix.
